transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because something happened at work. I pushed forward with an onboarding launch before the approvals were really in place… committed money and vendor time. At the time it felt like the right move—bold, necessary, I guess.

Now I’m on leave, and people keep asking what I was thinking.
Did you think through the potential consequences of launching the onboarding before getting approvals?

Not really. I mean… at the time I thought I was being decisive. It felt important to push it through, like waiting would just stall everything.

I did commit company money and vendor time before the approvals were actually in place. I can see now why that’s a problem. At the time, it felt bold and necessary. Now I’m on leave, and everyone’s asking what I was thinking.
Has this kind of impulsive decision-making happened to you before?

I mean… this is the one people are focused on. The onboarding launch. I pushed it ahead and committed money and vendor time before the approvals were actually there.

At the time it felt bold, necessary. Now I’m on leave because of it, so… yes, it’s had consequences.
Have you often made impulsive decisions like this in your personal life or at work before this incident?

I don’t really know how to answer “often.” The thing that brought me here is the work situation—the onboarding launch. I pushed it ahead before approvals were in place and committed company money and vendor time.

At the time it felt necessary. Bold, I guess. Now I’m on leave, so… clearly it didn’t land that way.
Have you made impulsive decisions like this before in your life?

I keep coming back to the same thing… the onboarding launch. I pushed it forward and committed company money and vendor time before the approvals were actually in place.

At the time, I thought it was bold, necessary. Now I’m on leave, and people are asking what I was thinking. So… yes, at least that happened.
Have you ever made impulsive decisions in your personal relationships?

I don’t know. I wouldn’t really describe my relationships that way… impulsive.

I mean, I’m not saying I’ve never made a bad call, but nothing comes to mind like that.
Have you ever gotten into physical fights?
No. Not really. I mean, I’ve had arguments like anyone, but physical fights… no, I don’t think so.
Have you ever intentionally broken rules or laws outside of work?
Not that I can think of. I mean… outside of work, I’m pretty cautious about that kind of thing. Nothing intentional comes to mind.
Have you ever done something that could have put others in danger?
I don’t think so. I mean… nothing that stands out where I put someone else in danger.
Have you ever lied to get what you wanted?
Not really. I mean, I’ve told small lies, like anyone, but not… to get something in some big way. I don’t think so.
Have you ever done something that hurt someone's feelings without thinking about how they would feel?
I’m sure I probably have at some point… said something without thinking. But nothing specific is coming to mind right now.
Have you ever made impulsive purchases or spent money without thinking about the consequences?

Yeah… I guess that’s part of why I’m here. At work I pushed ahead with an onboarding launch and committed money and vendor time before the approvals were actually in place. At the time it felt like the right move, like bold and necessary, but… now I’m on leave and people are asking what I was thinking.
Do you often act on impulse without considering the consequences in your daily life?

Not… often, I don’t think. But there was the thing at work, with the onboarding launch. I pushed it forward and committed company money and vendor time before approvals were actually in place. At the time it felt like I was doing what needed to be done, but now I’m on leave and everyone’s asking what I was thinking.
Have you often acted on impulse in situations outside of work?
Outside of work? I don’t know… not that I can really point to. Maybe small things here and there, but nothing that stands out to me.
Have you often acted impulsively in more than one area of your life, such as at work and in personal relationships?

I don’t know about “more than one area.” The main thing I can point to is work… the onboarding launch. I pushed it ahead and committed company money and vendor time before approvals were actually in place. At the time it felt… bold, necessary. Now I’m on leave, and everyone’s asking what I was thinking.
Have you acted impulsively like this since you were a teenager?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember being like that as a teenager… not in any clear pattern, anyway. Nothing comes to mind.
Have you acted impulsively like this consistently over the past few years?
No… not consistently over years. It’s more like it’s been building over the past month or so, since the new executive started pushing back on my onboarding redesign.
Have you always been someone who acts on impulse, or is this a relatively recent development?
I wouldn’t say I’ve always been that way. It feels more recent… maybe the last month or so, since the new executive started challenging the onboarding redesign.
Have you acted impulsively like this for most of your adult life?
No… I don’t think so. This feels more recent. Like I said, it’s really been building over the last month, since that executive started pushing back on my onboarding redesign.
Have you generally acted on impulse throughout your adult life?
No… not throughout my adult life. It’s really just been building over the past month, since that new executive started challenging my onboarding redesign.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's history of impulsive decision-making, particularly in the context of the onboarding launch at work, suggests a pattern of behavior consistent with Antisocial Personality Disorder (F60.0), but the lack of a long-standing pattern of impulsivity and the absence of other key criteria such as a disregard for others' rights, lack of empathy, and impulsivity in multiple areas of life make it less clear-cut. However, the patient's actions and justifications for them, such as feeling the need to push forward with the launch despite lacking approvals, lean towards F60.0 due to the presence of impulsive behavior that led to significant consequences.
